findings.claim: The supplied router and capability catalog agree on six admitted foundation procedures: identity.session, identity.scopes, identity.entry and identity.syncCredentials are queries; identity.createInitialBond and authority.refreshSnapshot are commands. All six catalog entries admit only the app channel, require session assurance and declare G2 as required evidence. Required evidence is not proof that G2 has passed; the catalog explicitly leaves owner confirmation of that bar pending.

The router requires both identity and platform context before handling these procedures. The syncCredentials handler reports SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE when its issuer is absent. This establishes source-level wiring and guards, not observed runtime authentication or dependency behavior.

The catalog description's unqualified 'empty v1 contract' statement is stale relative to the six wired foundation procedures. Its narrower 'empty business contract' and 'empty business router' descriptions remain consistent with the supplied router: admitted identity and authority foundations do not constitute business feature admission. Historical pre-reset evidence still cannot establish current execution.

The governing policy's factual description of 'two read-only identity procedures' also needs updating: the supplied current surface contains six procedures, including two commands and an authority namespace. Its normative scope remains horizontal foundation, with business admission deferred and product decisions unreplaced by engineering guidance.

Resuming foundation work does not authorize implementing business procedures or migrating features. The policy explicitly defers business admission and unresolved product-policy choices; the catalog likewise treats feature/domain admission and capability-specific reconciliation as later work. Existing foundation commands do not imply general business authorization.
